tools.name: accept_dispute_claim
tools.description:
Accept liability for a dispute claim.

This tool is used to accept liability for a dispute claim. When you accept liability for a dispute claim, the dispute closes in the customer's favor and PayPal automatically refunds money to the customer from the merchant's account.

note.description: A note about why the seller is accepting the claim

tools.name: activate_recurring_series
tools.description:
Activate a recurring invoice series on PayPal.

This function activates a recurring invoice series by its ID, moving it out of DRAFT status. Once activated, PayPal automatically generates and sends invoices to the customer based on the series' configured schedule. Call this after create_recurring_series to make the series active.

recurring_series_id.description: The ID of the recurring invoice series to activate.

tools.name: cancel_invoice_auto_reminder
tools.description:
Cancel all scheduled automatic reminders for an invoice.

This function permanently cancels every automatic reminder scheduled for a specific invoice, by invoice ID. This action is irreversible -- once cancelled, automatic reminders cannot be re-enabled for that invoice.

invoice_id.description: The ID of the invoice for which to cancel all scheduled automatic reminders.

tools.name: cancel_recurring_series
tools.description:
Cancel a recurring invoice series on PayPal.

This function cancels a recurring invoice series by its ID. Once cancelled, PayPal stops generating and sending further invoices for the series. This action cannot be undone.

recurring_series_id.description: The ID of the recurring invoice series to cancel.

tools.name: cancel_sent_invoice
tools.description:
Cancel a sent invoice.

This function cancels an invoice that has already been sent to the recipient(s).

invoice_id.description: The ID of the invoice to cancel.

note.description: A cancellation note to the recipient.

send_to_recipient.description: Indicates whether to send the cancellation to the recipient.

additional_recipients.description: Additional email addresses to which to send the cancellation.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.description:
Cancel a customer subscription in PayPal.

This function cancels an active subscription for a customer. It requires the subscription ID and an optional reason for cancellation.
Required parameters are: subscription_id (the ID of the subscription to be canceled).
Below is the payload request structure:
{
    "reason": "Customer requested cancellation"
}
You MUST ask the user for: 
 - subscription_id
 - reason for cancellation.

Return all of the above as structured JSON in your response.

subscription_id.description: The ID of the subscription to show details.

reason.description: The reason for the cancellation of a subscription.

tools.name: create_conditional_rules_for_invoice
tools.description: Create conditional rules for an invoice on PayPal.

invoice_id.description: The ID of the invoice for which the conditional rules are to be created.

conditional_rule_type.description: The type of conditional rule to apply to the invoice.

conditional_rule_value_type.description: The type of the conditional rule value. Required, and only applicable, when conditional_rule_type is EARLY_PAYMENT_DISCOUNT.

conditional_rule_value.description: The value of the conditional rule. Required, and only applicable, when conditional_rule_type is EARLY_PAYMENT_DISCOUNT. When conditional_rule_value_type is PERCENT, must be between 1 and 100.

rule_expiry_condition.description: When the conditional rule expires: a specific date, or a period relative to the invoice issue date.

condition_rule_end_date.description: The date the conditional rule expires, in yyyy-MM-dd format.

rule_expiry_terms.description: The expiry terms for the conditional rule.

rules.description: The list of conditional rules to create for the invoice.

tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description:
Create Invoices on PayPal.

This function creates a draft invoice, specifying a currency code, the invoicer's business information, one or more recipients to bill, and line items. Once created, the invoice can be sent to the customer for payment.

primary_recipients and items use PayPal's real nested shape (billing_info/shipping_info for recipients; unit_amount/tax/discount for items); other fields use a simplified flat shape.

invoice_number.description: The invoice number. If omitted, PayPal auto-increments from the last invoice number used.

invoice_date.description: The invoice date in yyyy-MM-DD format.

reference.description: A reference value, such as a purchase order number.

note.description: A note to the invoice recipient. Also appears on the invoice notification email.

invoicer_business_name.description: The business name of the invoicer.

invoicer_given_name.description: The first name of the invoicer.

invoicer_surname.description: The last name of the invoicer.

invoicer_email_address.description: The email address of the invoicer.

invoicer_address_line_1.description: The first line of the invoicer's address, for example, number and street.

invoicer_address_line_2.description: The second line of the invoicer's address, for example, suite or apartment number.

invoicer_city.description: The city, town, or village of the invoicer's address.

invoicer_state.description: The state or province of the invoicer's address.

invoicer_postal_code.description: The postal code of the invoicer's address.

invoicer_country_code.description: The two-character ISO 3166-1 country code of the invoicer's address (for example, US or GB).

address_line_2.description: The second line of the address, for example, suite or apartment number.

shipping_cost.description: The shipping cost for the invoice, in the invoice's currency_code.

pay_by_bank_exclusive_above_threshold.description: When true, PAY_BY_BANK becomes the only available payment method once the invoice total exceeds PayPal's system-defined threshold ($1000), disabling all other payment methods above that threshold.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description:
Create an order in PayPal.

This tool is used to create a new order in PayPal. This is typically the first step in initiating a payment flow. It sets up an order with specified details such as item(s) to be purchased, quantity, amount, currency, and other details.

quantity.description: The item quantity. Must be a whole number.

itemCost.description: The cost of each item - upto 2 decimal points.

taxPercent.description: The tax percent for the specific item.

itemTotal.description: The total cost of this line item.

discount.description: The discount amount for the order.

shippingCost.description: The cost of shipping for the order.

address_line_1.description: The first line of the address, such as number and street, for example, `173 Drury Lane`.This field needs to pass the full address.

address_line_2.description: The second line of the address, for example, a suite or apartment number.

admin_area_2.description: A city, town, or village. Smaller than `admin_area_level_1`.

admin_area_1.description: The highest-level sub-division in a country, which is usually a province, state, or ISO-3166-2 subdivision.

postal_code.description: The postal code, which is the ZIP code or equivalent. Typically required for countries with a postal code or an equivalent.

country_code.description: The 2-character ISO 3166-1 code that identifies the country or region. Note: The country code for Great Britain is `GB` and not `UK` as used in the top-level domain names for that country.

anyOf.description: The shipping address for the order.

shippingAddress.description: The shipping address for the order.

tools.name: create_product
tools.description:
Create a product in PayPal using product catalog - create products API.
This function creates a new product that will be used in subscription plans, subscriptions.
Required parameters are: name (product name), type (product type).
High level: 
    - id: (auto-generated or specify SKU of the product) The ID of the product
    - name: {product_name} (required) 
    - description: {product_description} (optional)
    - type {DIGITAL | PHYSICAL | SERVICE} (required)
    - category: {product_category} (optional) 
    - image_url: {image_url} (optional)
    - home_url: {home_url} (optional)

Below is the payload request structure:
{
    "id": "#PROD-XYAB12ABSB7868434",
    "name": "Video Streaming Service",
    "description": "Service for streaming latest series, movies etc.",
    "type": "SERVICE",
    "category": "SOFTWARE",
    "image_url": "https://example.com/streaming.jpg",
    "home_url": "https://example.com/home"
}

type.description: The product type. Value is PHYSICAL, DIGITAL, or SERVICE.

image_url.description: The image URL for the product.

home_url.description: The home page URL for the product.

This function creates a recurring invoice series that automatically generates and sends invoices to a customer on a schedule, specifying a billing frequency, a start date, a currency code, a primary recipient, and line items for the series template.

tools.name: create_refund
tools.description:
Initiate a refund for a PayPal payment capture.
If you have an order ID instead of a capture ID, first use the get order tool to obtain the capture ID from the order details.
This function allows you to return funds to a customer by refunding a previously captured payment. You can issue a full refund or specify a partial amount. If multiple captures exist for an order, request clarification on which specific capture to refund.
Required parameters:
- Capture ID: The ID of the capture to refund
- Amount (optional): For partial refunds, specify the amount to refund (must be less than or equal to the captured amount)
- Note to Payer (optional): Additional explanation visible to the customer
Response details include:
- Refund ID and status
- Refunded amount and currency

capture_id.description: The ID of the capture to refund.

amount.description: The amount to refund. If not specified, the full captured amount is refunded.

invoice_id.description: The invoice ID that is used to track this payment.

tools.name: create_shipment_tracking
tools.description:
Create a shipment for a transaction in PayPal.
This function creates a shipment record for a specific transaction, allowing you to track the shipment status and details.
The transaction_id can fetch from the captured payment details in the order information.
Required parameters are: tracking_number (the tracking number for the shipment), transaction_id (the transaction ID associated with the shipment). 
High level: tracking_number, transaction_id, status (optional), carrier (optional) are required json objects.
Below is the payload request structure:
{
    "tracking_number": "1234567890",
    "transaction_id": "9XJ12345ABC67890",
    "status": "SHIPPED", // Required: ON_HOLD, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, CANCELLED
    "carrier": "UPS" // Required: The carrier handling the shipment. Link to supported carriers: http://developer.paypal.com/docs/tracking/reference/carriers/
}

order_id.description: The ID of the order for which to create a shipment

tracking_number.description: The tracking number for the shipment. Id is provided by the shipper. This is required to create a shipment.

transaction_id.description: The transaction ID associated with the shipment. Transaction id available after the order is paid or captured. This is required to create a shipment.

status.description: The status of the shipment. It can be "ON_HOLD", "SHIPPED", "DELIVERED", or "CANCELLED".

tools.name: create_subscription
tools.description:
Create a subscription in PayPal using the subscription - create subscription API.
This function allows you to create a new subscription for a specific plan, enabling the management of recurring payments.
The only required parameter is plan_id (the ID of the subscription plan). All other fields are optional and can be omitted if not provided.
The subscriber field is optional. If no subscriber information is provided, omit the subscriber field in the request payload.
The shipping address is optional. If no shipping address is provided, set the shipping_preference to GET_FROM_FILE in the application context.
The application context is also optional. If no application context information is provided, omit the application context field in the request payload.

plan_id.description: The ID of the subscription plan to create.

quantity.description: The quantity of the product in the subscription.

currency_code.description: The currency code for the shipping amount.

value.description: The value of the shipping amount.

shipping_amount.description: The shipping amount for the subscription.

address_line_1.description: The first line of the address.

address_line_2.description: The second line of the address.

return_url.description: The return URL after the subscription is created.

cancel_url.description: The cancel URL if the user cancels the subscription.

payer_selected.description: The payment method selected by the payer.

payee_preferred.description: The preferred payment method for the payee.

application_context.description: The application context for the subscription.

tools.name: create_subscription_plan
tools.description:
Create a subsctiption plan in PayPal using subscription - create plan API.
This function creates a new subscription plan that defines pricing and billing cycle details for subscriptions.
Required parameters are: product_id (the ID of the product for which to create the plan), name (subscription plan name), billing_cycles (billing cycle details).
High level: product_id, name, description, taxes, status: {CREATED|INACTIVE|ACTIVE}, billing_cycles, payment_preferences are required in json object.
While creating billing_cycles object, trial(second) billing cycle should precede regular billing cycle.

product_id.description: The ID of the product for which to create the plan.

interval_unit.description: The unit of time for the billing cycle.

interval_count.description: The number of units for the billing cycle.

frequency.description: The frequency of the billing cycle.

tenure_type.description: The type of billing cycle tenure.

sequence.description: The sequence of the billing cycle.

total_cycles.description: The total number of cycles in the billing plan.

currency_code.description: The currency code for the fixed price.

value.description: The value of the fixed price.

fixed_price.description: The fixed price for the subscription plan.

version.description: The version of the pricing scheme.

pricing_scheme.description: The pricing scheme for the billing cycle.

billing_cycles.description: The billing cycles of the plan.

auto_bill_outstanding.description: Indicates whether to automatically bill outstanding amounts.

currency_code.description: The currency code for the setup fee.

value.description: The value of the setup fee.

setup_fee.description: The setup fee for the subscription plan.

setup_fee_failure_action.description: The action to take if the setup fee payment fails.

payment_failure_threshold.description: The number of failed payments before the subscription is canceled.

payment_preferences.description: The payment preferences for the subscription plan.

inclusive.description: Indicates whether the tax is inclusive.

tools.name: delete_invoice
tools.description:
Delete a draft or scheduled invoice on PayPal.

This function permanently deletes an invoice that is in the draft or scheduled state, by ID. It does not work on invoices that have already been sent -- use cancel_sent_invoice for those instead. After deletion, the invoice's details can no longer be retrieved, but its invoice number can be reused.

invoice_id.description: The ID of the draft or scheduled invoice to delete.

tools.name: delete_recurring_series
tools.description:
Delete a recurring invoice series on PayPal.

This function permanently deletes a recurring invoice series by its ID. Only series in DRAFT status can be deleted -- for a series that has already been activated, use cancel_recurring_series instead. This action cannot be undone.

recurring_series_id.description: The ID of the recurring invoice series to delete. Only series in DRAFT status can be deleted; use cancel_recurring_series for an activated series.

tools.name: generate_invoice_number
tools.description:
Generate the next invoice number available to the merchant.

This function generates the next invoice number by using the prefix and suffix from the merchant's last invoice number and incrementing the numeric portion by one (e.g. INVOICE-1234 -> INVOICE-1235).

tools.name: generate_invoice_qr_code
tools.description:
Generate a QR code for an invoice.

This function generates a QR code for an invoice, which can be used to pay the invoice using a mobile device or scanning app.

invoice_id.description: The invoice id to generate QR code for

tools.name: get_dispute
tools.description:
Get details for a specific dispute from PayPal.

This tool is used to lists disputes with a summary set of details, which shows the dispute_id, reason, status, dispute_state, dispute_life_cycle_stage, dispute_channel, dispute_amount, create_time and update_time fields.

dispute_id.description: The order id generated during create call

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description:
Get an invoice from PayPal.

This function retrieves details of a specific invoice using its ID.

invoice_id.description: The ID of the invoice to retrieve.

tools.name: get_merchant_insights
tools.description:
Retrieve business intelligence metrics and analytics for a merchant, filtered by start date, end date, insight type, and time interval.

This tool returns actionable insights into orders and sales data, supporting data-driven business decisions.

start_date.description: The start date range to filter insights

end_date.description: The end date range to filter insights

insight_type.description: The type of insight to retrieve. It can be "ORDERS" or "SALES"

time_interval.description: The time periods used for segmenting metrics data. It can be "DAILY", "WEEKLY", "MONTHLY", "QUARTERLY", or "YEARLY"

tools.name: get_order
tools.description:
Retrieves the order details from PayPal for a given order ID.

This tool is used to retrieve details of an existing order in PayPal. It provides information about the order, including items, amounts, status, and other relevant details.

id.description: The order id generated during create call

tools.name: get_recurring_series
tools.description:
Get a recurring invoice series from PayPal.

This function retrieves details of a specific recurring invoice series using its ID, including its schedule, status, template, and recipient information.

recurring_series_id.description: The ID of the recurring invoice series to retrieve.

tools.name: get_refund
tools.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a PayPal payment refund.
If you have an order ID instead of a refund ID, first use the get order tool to obtain the refund ID from the order details. 
This function returns comprehensive details about a refund, including its current status (completed, pending, cancelled), refunded amount, and processing information.
When multiple refunds exist for an order or capture, request clarification on which specific refund to retrieve. 
Response details include:
- Refund status and ID
- Refunded amount and currency
- Reason for refund (if provided)
- Source transaction details

refund_id.description: The ID of the refund to get details for.

tools.name: get_shipment_tracking
tools.description:
Get tracking information for a shipment by ID.
This function retrieves tracking information for a specific shipment using the transaction ID and tracking number.
The transaction_id can fetch from the captured payment details in the order information.
Below is the payload request structure:

order_id.description: The ID of the order for which to create a shipment.

transaction_id.description: The transaction ID associated with the shipment tracking to retrieve.

tools.name: list_disputes
tools.description:
List disputes from PayPal.

This function retrieves a list of disputes with optional pagination and filtering parameters.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description:
List invoices from PayPal.

This function retrieves a list of invoices with optional pagination parameters.

page.description: The page number of the result set to fetch.

page_size.description: The number of records to return per page (maximum 100).

total_required.description: Indicates whether the response should include the total count of items.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description:
List products from PayPal.

This function retrieves a list of products with optional pagination parameters.

page.description: The page number of the result set to fetch.

page_size.description: The number of records to return per page (maximum 100).

total_required.description: Indicates whether the response should include the total count of products.

tools.name: list_subscription_plans
tools.description:
List subscription plans from PayPal.

This function retrieves a list of subscription plans with optional product filtering and pagination parameters.

product_id.description: The ID of the product for which to get subscription plans.

page.description: The page number of the result set to fetch.

page_size.description: The number of records to return per page (maximum 100).

total_required.description: Indicates whether the response should include the total count of plans.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.description:
List transactions from PayPal.

This tool is used to list transactions with optional filtering parameters within a date range of 31 days. This tool can also be used to list details of a transaction given the transaction ID.

- The start_date and end_date should be specified in ISO8601 date and time format. Example dates: 1996-12-19T16:39:57-08:00, 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, 1990-12-31T23:59:60Z
- The transaction_status accepts the following 4 values:
    1. "D" - represents denied transactions.
